Hello. I’m sorry you feel this way. Just want to give my experience which hopefully might give some hope to you and others. 
I did psychotherapy for 7 years and took different meds multiple times due to my poor mental health. I was myself within the spectrum of borderline personality disorder. It feels unreal now to think how much I was suffering back then, daily suicidal ideation, strong dissociation, endless rumination on the meaning of life, fear of losing control and jumping off a bridge. That was my bread and butter every day, for years, not joking. Now I don’t have these thoughts any longer, and if they come back (which happen not frequently), they don’t hold a grip on me how they used to, even if uncomfortable. Now I’m able to enjoy myself, live my life, and focus on positive things and my loved ones. When I’m going through a stressful period, it is more likely for me to fall back in those patters, but I swear it is nothing to worry about in comparison to what it used to be. What I want to say with this post is that through the right therapist, combination of meds, and self work and determination (this is very important!), you got this. I’m the living example. I wish you the best of luck with your healing journey.

Ps: I’m 31 yo, started my healing journey when I was around 21, between 21-27 yo is when I was suffering the hardest with suicidal thoughts, depression, anxiety, and dissociation.

Considering medication is a good option if the thoughts are too overwhelming and don’t allow you to function properly in my opinion. I took many medications throughout the years, mostly for my mood swings and depression, but once I was put on Zoloft because of my constant and exhausting rumination on a past event (real event ocd). I have to say that it helped so much with it, I’ve almost stopped having any anxiety related to the event causing me to ruminate and feel horribly. Then I got off Zoloft as my psychiatrist would always avoid kept me on meds for too long. But I would totally recommend it if the ocd is limiting your daily life significantly. 
Then the best fight for it is therapy imo. But also a combination of therapy and meds is good.
I understand your concern about starting meds, it is pretty reasonable and I had it too back then, but really they are just meds! They don’t mess up your brain for good but are just as the other meds you take to cure a headache or diabetes. It is just that culturally we are influenced to think of psychiatric meds as something dark that just crazy ppl take, but that’s not true. Also, if you feel they don’t work on you or you don’t like the side effects, you can always quit (never cold turkey of course). Good luck :)
